_comment: THE NUMBERS IN THIS FILE ARE CONSERVATIVE AND UNVALIDATED.
BRIEF.md deliberately fixes no threshold and CLAUDE.md rule 8 forbids
inventing one and then treating it as decided. Every value here exists so
that a setting EXISTS and is enforced; none of them has been checked
against how this system actually behaves over weeks, because it has not
run for weeks yet. Change them deliberately, in a commit that says why.
Keys beginning with an underscore are comments and are ignored by the
loader. Every other key is required: the dashboard has no built-in default
and refuses to start on a file that is missing one.
bindAddress is LOOPBACK. This is the first listening socket this system
has ever had, and the page behind it renders vendor refusal details that
are derived from URLs carrying a credential in the query string. This must
be a literal IP address, and the loader REFUSES the unspecified address in
either family however it is spelled - it parses the value and looks at its
bytes, because 0.0.0.0, ::, ::0, ::ffff:0.0.0.0 and 0 are one address
written five ways and this runtime binds all five to every interface. A
name is refused as well: a resolver answers at listen time and what it
answers is not what this file said. A specific LAN address is permitted if
the owner puts one here deliberately; there is no authentication, no TLS
and no accounts, so anything that can reach the socket sees everything.
stalenessHorizonMs is how old a source's most recent SUCCESSFUL fetch may
be before the page reports that source as BROKEN. 48 hours: the collection
cadence is the owner's and is not fixed anywhere in this repository, so
the horizon is set well past a daily run rather than tuned to one. Too
long and a dead source reads as quiet, which is the failure the roadmap
phase's fail-safe names; too short and everything reads broken and nobody
looks twice. Nobody has lived with this system long enough to know the
right number - this one is a starting point to be moved, not a finding.
ratePeriodMs is what the success, error and block rates on the overview
are computed over: 24 hours, matching the allowance period the governor is
configured with, so the two halves of the page describe the same day.
defaultChartRangeMs is how much of a listing's history the chart shows
when nobody has asked for a range: 90 days, which is the window the brief
talks about historical lows over.
conditionHistoryLimit is how many recent conditions, pauses and stops a
source's detail lists. Bounded so that one badly behaved source cannot
make the page enormous.
